Decision map: delay length × surroundings during the delay

Why does it warm this way?

Model A treats the package as one temperature that drifts toward the surroundings. The time constant $\tau$ says how slowly: a larger $\tau$ means slower warming.

$$\frac{dT}{dt}=\frac{T_a-T}{\tau}\quad\Rightarrow\quad H(s)=\frac{1}{\tau s+1},\qquad s_p=-\frac{1}{\tau}$$

Model B separates the container from the payload, so heat reaches the payload more slowly.

$$H(s)=\frac{1}{R_oR_iC_cC_p\,s^2+\left(R_oC_c+R_oC_p+R_iC_p\right)s+1}$$

What is $H(s)$? It describes how the model reacts to a change in surroundings, starting from equilibrium. A real journey starts at a given temperature $T_0$, so we add that in: $$Y(s)=\frac{T_a(s)+\tau T_0}{\tau s+1}$$ For constant surroundings, $T_a(s)=T_a/s$, and this inverts to $T(t)=T_a+(T_0-T_a)e^{-t/\tau}$. The simulator uses this one stage at a time and passes the end temperature to the next stage. The pole sits at $-1/\tau$: the closer it is to zero, the slower the response.

The decision margin is the time until the limit minus the time still needed. A positive margin means arrival within range. $$t_{\lim}=\tau\ln\frac{T_a-T_0}{T_a-T_{\lim}},\qquad \text{margin}=t_{\lim}-t_{\text{remaining}}$$

Reading the graphs. Height is how strongly the model responds at $s=\sigma+i\omega$. The red dashed line marks where the Laplace integral converges (to its right); the surface on its left is the same formula extended. Points next to a pole are hidden because the value blows up there.

Limits. The model assumes steady properties, one uniform temperature per part, no ice or phase change, and surroundings we choose. Results compare predicted temperature with a range. They do not judge drug stability or safety. Parameters are assumed unless fitted on the Investigate page (open-beaker water data only).

Truck model: “LCT 3000 ’95 - Low poly model” (https://skfb.ly/pALNn) by Daniel Zhabotinsky, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Body colour and finish modified in this demonstrator to indicate payload status.

Constant thermal properties, uniform temperatures, no phase change, prescribed surroundings. Outputs are predicted temperatures against a chosen range, not pharmaceutical stability or clinical safety judgements. Sensitivity ranges are not confidence intervals. Parameters are labelled Assumed unless fitted from data in the Investigate page (open-beaker educational data only).
